subjective: Blackie, a Shih Tzu, is walking but appears weak and in pain. The owner reports that Blackie has a history of joint issues and weighs approximately 40 kg. The owner notes that Blackie sometimes shows discomfort when eating and licks himself excessively. Recently, Blackie had a day when he did not eat and had reduced drinking strength, but currently is eating. Despite pain, Blackie enjoys coming to the clinic. The owner is concerned about the limb condition and joint health.
objective: Physical palpation of the affected limb is limited due to pain and inability to assess skin abnormalities or swelling. No samples or diagnostic imaging have been performed yet. The veterinarian suggests the need for diagnostic tests including X-rays and possibly blood sugar tests. No vital signs or specific measurements were recorded during this consultation.
assessment: Blackie is experiencing limb pain with possible joint involvement. The exact condition of the limb is unclear due to limited palpation and lack of diagnostic imaging. There is concern for progression of joint issues, potentially exacerbated by Blackie's weight. Pain management is necessary. Further diagnostics are required to rule out other factors affecting the limb and to assess the contralateral limb.
plan: 1. Administer an injection to reduce pain and observe Blackie for one day. 2. Schedule diagnostic tests including X-rays of the affected limb and possibly the other limb to rule out additional issues. 3. Consider blood sugar testing to assess systemic health. 4. Use a splint or plastic support if indicated, to be removed after some time depending on progress. 5. Initiate therapy post stabilization, including possible medications or formulations to support joint health. 6. Advise weight management to reduce joint stress. 7. Monitor appetite and drinking; if no improvement after one day, reassess and consider further interventions. 8. Owner to continue bringing Blackie for follow-up visits as scheduled.
conclusion: Blackie, a Shih Tzu with a history of joint issues and weighing approximately 40 kg, presents with limb pain and weakness. Physical examination is limited due to pain, and no diagnostic imaging or samples have been obtained yet. Pain management was initiated with an injection, and further diagnostics including X-rays and blood sugar testing are planned to evaluate the limb condition and rule out other factors. Weight management is recommended to mitigate joint stress. The owner reports intermittent decreased appetite and drinking but notes Blackie is currently eating and enjoys clinic visits despite pain. Follow-up and monitoring are advised to assess response to treatment and progression of symptoms.
key_issues: 1. Limb pain and weakness with unclear etiology due to limited examination. 2. Chronic joint issues potentially exacerbated by overweight status (40 kg). 3. Pain management and need for diagnostic imaging to clarify diagnosis.
abnormal_findings: Pain on limb palpation limiting examination. Reduced appetite and drinking noted on one occasion. Excessive licking behavior reported previously.

Report any worsening of symptoms or lack of improvement promptly.
reminders: Reassess Blackie after one day of pain management. Schedule and perform diagnostic imaging and blood tests. Monitor clinical signs and adjust treatment accordingly. Follow-up visits to evaluate joint status and response to therapy.
